## Overview

In WRITE mode, `MoRIIOConnector` assumes one prefill rank per TP index that writes every layer. With pipeline parallelism, the index is shared for the stages, so the stages collide on ports and the later ones fail to start. Each stage also numbers its layers from zero, so a stage that does write puts them on the decode instance's first layers. This PR lets a prefill instance under MoRIIO's WRITE mode use pipeline parallelism, with each stage writing the layers it holds to the decode addresses of those same layers and a decode rank finishing the transfer only after every stage has reported.



## Claims

- A prefill instance can now run with pipeline parallelism in WRITE mode. Each stage writes its own layers, and decoding starts only after every stage has reported.
- For MLA models the main gain is prefill capacity. On GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 (8 × MI355X), a TP1 × PP4 prefill instance holds about 4× the KV cache of a TP4 one (4.12× and 4.02×) and serves 41.9 % and 27.1 % more tokens per GPU on 32K-token prompts at 16 concurrent requests, with TTFT p50 down 42 % and 30 %.
- The peer's layer addresses are now looked up by layer name. This also fixes a case without pipeline parallelism where a decode instance with an MTP layer is fed by a prefill instance without MTP.
- Combinations the connector don't support fail at startup with an error that articulates the setting.



## Validation

### Unit tests

The new tests added are CPU tests in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_pipeline_parallel.py` (21 cases, `cpu_test`), ROCm + MoRI cases in `test_moriio_connector.py` (per-stage ports and MoRI engine keys, refused PP roles and layouts), and one case in `test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py` (the handshake advertises each layer's region). Reverting each part of the change to main's behaviour makes its tests fail.

| Behaviours | Tests | Main | With this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Peer layer address by local position | `test_peer_with_an_extra_draft_layer_is_addressed_by_name`, `test_stage_writes_each_layer_at_the_peer_address_of_that_layer` | 2 failed | 2 passed |
| Port offset without the stage term | `test_every_stage_worker_binds_its_own_ports` | 3 failed, 1 passed (no PP) | 4 passed |
| First stage does not forward the decode's messages | test_every_stage_gets_the_allocation_and_release | 3 failed | 3 passed |
| Decode counts `write_done` messages, not senders | `test_decode_rank_waits_for_every_distinct_stage` | 1 failed | 1 passed |
| Producer `num_writers` without the stage count | `test_stage_reports_every_stage_as_a_writer_and_names_itself` | 1 failed | 1 passed |
| Consumer does not mark a settled transfer | `test_first_stage_failure_fails_the_transfer_once` | 1 failed | 1 passed |

### End-to-end verification with GLM-5.2/GLM-5.3

These runs use a single node of 8 MI355X GPUs, with the prefill instance on GPUs 0-3 and a TP4 decode instance on GPUs 4-7, MoRIIO WRITE over xGMI and the toy proxy from vLLM example. Both instances use block size 64, fp8 KV and index caches, MTP with 3 speculative tokens, prefix caching, chunked prefill at 32,768 tokens, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs, the glm47 parsers and thinking on, with `--max-num-seqs 256`. The TP1 × PP4 prefill instances use `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=22,20,20,16`. Note that the runs below includes #64330, which fixes the completion-wait hang over xGMI.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.2 | TP4 | 2,622,592 | | 0.9340 / 0.9348 |3,220 | | 16.01 | | 19.86 | |
| GLM-5.2 | TP1 × PP4 | 10,817,536 | +312 | 0.9325 / 0.9333 |4,568 | +41.9 | 9.35 | −41.6 | 19.76 | −0.5 |
| GLM-5.3 | TP4 | 2,753,664 | | 0.9689 / 0.9689 | 2,977 | | 17.64 | | 21.44 | |
| GLM-5.3 | TP1 × PP4 | 11,079,424 | +302 | 0.9674 / 0.9682 | 3,783 | +27.1 | 12.30 | −30.3 | 23.30 | +8.7 |

Throughput is per GPU over all eight GPUs, on 128 prompts, and every request completed without a preemption. vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --served-model-name GLM-5.2 --port 8002 --tensor-parallel-size 4 $COMMON \
```bash
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MoRIIOConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backend":"xgmi","read_mode":"false","proxy_ip":"127.0.0.1","proxy_ping_port":"8003","http_port":"8002","handshake_port":"8026","notify_port":"8034"}}'

  --model_args "model=GLM-5.2,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_gen_toks=16384,max_retries=3,timeout=3600" \

# benchmark
```

## Details

For MLA models, a TP*n* prefill instance keeps a full copy of each layer's latent KV on every TP rank. Splitting the layers across pipeline stages instead lets the same GPUs hold up to *n* times the tokens, which is what makes a TP1 × PP4 prefill instance attractive for models like GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3.

With this PR, a WRITE transfer from a pipeline-parallel prefill instance goes through four steps.
1. The decode scheduler sends the block allocation (and, on a full prefix hit or an abort, the release) to the notify ports of the first stage, as for a pipeline-free prefill instance.
2. Each worker of the first stage forwards every message from the decode to the same worker of the later stages on its node.
3. Each stage writes the layers it holds into those blocks, at the decode addresses of the same layers.
4. Each stage sends `write_done`, and a decode rank finishes the transfer after the last one.

On main none of this holds. Every stage binds the same handshake and notify ports and registers the same MoRI engine key, so stage 1 fails to start. The decode side only notifies `range(prefill_tp)` ports, so with TP1 only stage 0 ever learns the decode blocks. And the peer's layer address comes from this worker's own registration order.

```
vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py's MoRIIOConnectorWorker._remote_layer_mr_offset
idx = self.layer_base_addr_index[layer_name]
...
return remote_moriio_meta.kv_caches_base_addr[idx] - mr_base
```

So stage `s` writes its first layer at the decode's layer 0. On top of that, a decode rank finishes after `num_writers` messages, and `num_writers` comes from the TP mapping alone (1 for prefill TP1 → decode TP4), so it would start decoding after the first stage.

The layer lookup is also wrong without pipeline parallelism whenever the two instances register different layers. vLLM's KV planner groups layers by spec and puts a draft layer in its target's group, so for DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 the decode's MTP latent cache sits after the target latents and before every indexer cache. A prefill instance without MTP then silently writes indexer cache 0 into the decode's MTP region, and indexer cache `j` into region `j - 1`.

This PR makes the following changes.
- It adds a stage term to the port offset, `pp_rank * tp_size * dp_size_local`, so stage 0 keeps the ports of a pipeline-free instance, and it appends `:pp<rank>` to the MoRI engine key when PP > 1.
- It has each worker of the first stage forward the decode instance’s messages to the same worker of the later stages, so the decode instance and the router address the prefill instance as a pipeline-free one and need no pipeline size.
- It advertises `layer_base_addr_index` (layer name → region index) in the handshake and looks the peer's layers up by name. A peer without the field is only used when it registered the same number of regions, and otherwise the transfer fails with an error that names both counts.
- It sends `write_done` with `sender = [pp_rank, tp_rank]` and `num_writers` multiplied by `pp_size`. The decode rank counts distinct senders and marks the transfer settled, so late or repeated reports are dropped. Messages without a sender, from older peers, are counted per message, and a single writer's messages don't change.

Pipeline parallelism is only allowed on a WRITE-mode `kv_producer`. A READ-mode decode would have to read each layer from the stage that holds it, and a pipeline-parallel decode would need every producer to address its stages. A stage also refuses a block-outermost KV cache layout, because such a block packs every layer the worker holds, so its stride stops matching the decode's once a stage holds only some of the layers.

Notes:
- Over xGMI, main's completion wait can sleep out the full `transfer_timeout`, or fail with copies still in flight and send no `write_failed`. #64330 fixes the wait and the end-to-end runs were performed with the fix.
- GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 layers reuse the sparse-attention top-k of the nearest earlier indexer layer, so on main every pipeline stage must start on a layer that runs its own indexer (for GLM-5.2 at PP4, `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=22,20,20,16`).

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

`pp_size` is read here, but nothing sets it. `request_finished` returns `tp_size` (L1672) but not `pp_size`. So a router that forwards the prefill's returned `kv_transfer_params` to the decode (the serial-WRITE / llm-d path described in `update_state_after_alloc`) leaves the decode thinking the prefill has PP=1.

For a TP1 x PP4 prefill, the decode then notifies only `notify_port + 0`. Stages 1-3 never get the allocation, wait `defer_timeout` (60 s), and send `write_failed`, so every request fails. I checked this with the returned keys: `get_peer_notify_ports(...)` gives `[61005]`, while the stages bind `61005..61008`.

Suggested fix: add `pp_size=self.vllm_config.parallel_config.pipeline_parallel_size,` next to `tp_size=` in `request_finished`.

A stage running on another node gets past this check. The decode sends every stage's allocation and release to one host (`remote_host`, from rank 0's heartbeat). With TP8 x PP2 across two nodes, for example, stage 1 never receives its allocation, and each request fails after `defer_timeout`.

The PR aims to fail unsupported setups at startup, so consider also refusing `parallel_config.nnodes_within_dp > 1` here when PP > 1 (this covers the mp backend). The doc should also say that all stages must share a host.

Nit: these copies aren't needed. `_finalize_if_complete` already reads `self.worker.tp_rank` in the same dict, so `self.worker.pp_rank` / `self.worker.pp_size` would work there. That also removes the two extra lines in `make_moriio_writer` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py`.

```
idx = self.layer_base_addr_index[layer_name]
...
return remote_moriio_meta.kv_caches_base_addr[idx] - mr_base
```

So stage `s` writes its first layer at the decode's layer 0. On top of that, a decode rank finishes after `num_writers` messages, and `num_writers` comes from the TP mapping alone (1 for prefill TP1 → decode TP4), so it would start decoding after the first stage.

The layer lookup is also wrong without pipeline parallelism whenever the two instances register different layers. vLLM's KV planner groups layers by spec and puts a draft layer in its target's group, so for DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 the decode's MTP latent cache sits after the target latents and before every indexer cache. A prefill instance without MTP then silently writes indexer cache 0 into the decode's MTP region, and indexer cache `j` into region `j - 1`.

This PR makes the following changes.
- It adds a stage term to the port offset, `pp_rank * tp_size * dp_size_local`, so stage 0 keeps the ports of a pipeline-free instance, and it appends `:pp<rank>` to the MoRI engine key when PP > 1.
- It has each worker of the first stage forward the decode instance’s messages to the same worker of the later stages, so the decode instance and the router address the prefill instance as a pipeline-free one and need no pipeline size.
- It advertises `layer_base_addr_index` (layer name → region index) in the handshake and looks the peer's layers up by name. A peer without the field is only used when it registered the same number of regions, and otherwise the transfer fails with an error that names both counts.
- It sends `write_done` with `sender = [pp_rank, tp_rank]` and `num_writers` multiplied by `pp_size`. The decode rank counts distinct senders and marks the transfer settled, so late or repeated reports are dropped. Messages without a sender, from older peers, are counted per message, and a single writer's messages don't change.

Pipeline parallelism is only allowed on a WRITE-mode `kv_producer`. A READ-mode decode would have to read each layer from the stage that holds it, and a pipeline-parallel decode would need every producer to address its stages. A stage also refuses a block-outermost KV cache layout, because such a block packs every layer the worker holds, so its stride stops matching the decode's once a stage holds only some of the layers.

Notes:
- Over xGMI, main's completion wait can sleep out the full `transfer_timeout`, or fail with copies still in flight and send no `write_failed`. #64330 fixes the wait and the end-to-end runs were performed with the fix.
- GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 layers reuse the sparse-attention top-k of the nearest earlier indexer layer, so on main every pipeline stage must start on a layer that runs its own indexer (for GLM-5.2 at PP4, `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=22,20,20,16`).

+"""MoRIIO WRITE from a pipeline-parallel producer (e.g. P TP1 x PP4 -> D TP4)."""
+

+import socket
+import threading
+import time
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import msgspec
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.moriio import (
+    moriio_common,
+    moriio_engine,
+)

+    ROLE,
+    MoRIIOAgentMetadata,
+    MoRIIOConfig,
+    MoRIIOError,
+    MoRIIOMode,
+    RemoteAllocInfo,
+    get_port_offset,
+)

+    MoRIIOConnectorScheduler,
+    MoRIIOConnectorWorker,
+)

+    MoRIIOWrapper,
+)
+from vllm.v1.request import RequestStatus
+
+from .utils import make_moriio_writer
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test
+
+NOTIFY_PORT = 61005
+HANDSHAKE_PORT = 6301
+
+
+def _moriio_config(pp_rank, pp_size, tp_rank, tp_size, dp_rank=0, dp_size=1):
+    vllm_config = SimpleNamespace(
+        kv_transfer_config=SimpleNamespace(
+            kv_connector_extra_config={
+                "host_ip": "127.0.0.1",
+                "http_port": 8000,
+                "handshake_port": HANDSHAKE_PORT,
+                "notify_port": NOTIFY_PORT,
+            }
+        ),
+        parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(
+            data_parallel_rank=dp_rank,
+            data_parallel_size=dp_size,
+            data_parallel_size_local=dp_size,
+            pipeline_parallel_size=pp_size,
+        ),
+    )
+    with patch.multiple(
+        moriio_common,
+        get_tensor_model_parallel_rank=lambda: tp_rank,
+        get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size=lambda: tp_size,
+        get_pipeline_model_parallel_rank=lambda: pp_rank,
+    ):
+        return MoRIIOConfig.from_vllm_config(vllm_config)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("pp_size", "tp_size", "dp_size"),
+    [(1, 4, 1), (4, 1, 1), (2, 2, 1), (2, 1, 2)],
+)
+def test_every_stage_worker_binds_its_own_ports(pp_size, tp_size, dp_size):
+    configs = [
+        _moriio_config(pp, pp_size, tp, tp_size, dp, dp_size)
+        for pp, dp, tp in itertools.product(
+            range(pp_size), range(dp_size), range(tp_size)
+        )
+    ]
+
+    notify_ports = [config.notify_port for config in configs]
+    assert len(set(notify_ports)) == len(configs)
+    for config in configs:
+        assert config.notify_port == NOTIFY_PORT + config.port_offset
+        if config.pp_rank == 0:
+            # Stage 0 keeps the ports of a pipeline-free instance.
+            assert config.port_offset == get_port_offset(config.dp_rank, config.tp_rank)
+
+        # The first stage forwards to the same worker of every later stage.
+        later = [
+            other.notify_port
+            for other in configs
+            if other.pp_rank > 0
+            and (other.dp_rank, other.tp_rank) == (config.dp_rank, config.tp_rank)
+        ]
+        assert config.later_stage_notify_ports() == (
+            later if config.pp_rank == 0 else []
+        )
+
+
+def _decode_scheduler(*, send: bool = False) -> MoRIIOConnectorScheduler:
+    """A decode scheduler that records its notifications, or sends them."""
+    scheduler = MoRIIOConnectorScheduler.__new__(MoRIIOConnectorScheduler)
+    scheduler.mode = MoRIIOMode.WRITE
+    scheduler.is_producer = False
+    scheduler.tp_size = 4
+    scheduler._has_mamba = False
+    scheduler._is_hma_required = False
+    scheduler._is_kv_master = True
+    scheduler._global_dp_rank = 0
+    scheduler.transfer_id_to_request_id = {}
+    scheduler.request_id_to_transfer_id = {}
+    scheduler.paths = {}
+    scheduler.notified = []
+    scheduler.released = []
+    if not send:
+        scheduler.send_notify_block = (  # type: ignore[method-assign]
+            lambda **kwargs: scheduler.notified.append(kwargs)
+        )
+        scheduler._send_transfer_release = (  # type: ignore[method-assign]
+            lambda transfer_id, host, port: scheduler.released.append(port)
+        )
+    return scheduler
+
+
+def _prefill_scheduler(pp_size: int, tp_size: int, host: str, notify_port: int):
+    """The prefill-side state request_finished reads."""
+    scheduler = SimpleNamespace(
+        is_producer=True,
+        _is_hma_required=False,
+        _has_mamba=False,
+        blocks_per_sw=[0],
+        _global_dp_rank=0,
+        engine_id="prefill",
+        host_ip=host,
+        handshake_port=HANDSHAKE_PORT,
+        side_notify_port=notify_port,
+        vllm_config=SimpleNamespace(
+            parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(
+                data_parallel_size=1,
+                data_parallel_size_local=1,
+                tensor_parallel_size=tp_size,
+                pipeline_parallel_size=pp_size,
+            )
+        ),
+    )
+    scheduler.get_exchange_clipped_blocks = (
+        MoRIIOConnectorScheduler.get_exchange_clipped_blocks.__get__(scheduler)
+    )
+    return scheduler
+
+
+# The shapes of the decode request's kv_transfer_params a router can send. None
+# carries a pipeline size.
+PARAMS_SHAPES = ["peer sizes", "returned by prefill", "tp_size only"]
+
+
+def _decode_params(shape, pp_size, tp_size, host="10.0.0.1", notify_port=NOTIFY_PORT):
+    """The decode request's kv_transfer_params in one of PARAMS_SHAPES."""
+    if shape == "returned by prefill":
+        # What the prefill's request_finished returns, forwarded as is.
+        _, params = MoRIIOConnectorScheduler.request_finished(
+            _prefill_scheduler(pp_size, tp_size, host, notify_port),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+            SimpleNamespace(  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+                request_id="req",
+                kv_transfer_params={"do_remote_decode": True, "transfer_id": "tA"},
+                status=RequestStatus.FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED,
+            ),
+            block_ids=[],
+        )
+        assert params is not None
+        return params
+    params = {
+        "do_remote_prefill": True,
+        "transfer_id": "tA",
+        "remote_host": host,
+        "remote_notify_port": notify_port,
+        "remote_dp_size": 1,
+    }
+    if shape == "tp_size only":
+        # One TP size and a pinned DP rank, set by the router itself.
+        return {**params, "tp_size": tp_size, "remote_dp_rank": 0}
+    # The prefill's TP and DP sizes, as a router learns them from registration.
+    return {**params, "remote_tp_size": tp_size}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", PARAMS_SHAPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("pp_size", "tp_size"), [(4, 1), (2, 2)])
+def test_decode_addresses_only_the_first_stage(shape, pp_size, tp_size):
+    """The decode notifies a pipeline-parallel prefill as a pipeline-free one,
+    whatever params it gets; the first stage forwards to the others."""
+    params = _decode_params(shape, pp_size, tp_size)
+    first_stage = sorted(
+        _moriio_config(0, pp_size, tp, tp_size).notify_port for tp in range(tp_size)
+    )
+    scheduler = _decode_scheduler()
+
+    scheduler.update_state_after_alloc(
+        SimpleNamespace(request_id="req", kv_transfer_params=params),
+        SimpleNamespace(get_block_ids=lambda: ([5, 6, 7],)),
+        num_external_tokens=40,
+    )
+    scheduler._release_write_prefill_blocks("req", {**params, "remote_dp_rank": 0})
+
+    assert sorted(n["port"] for n in scheduler.notified) == first_stage
+    assert all(n["block_notify_list"] == [5, 6, 7] for n in scheduler.notified)
+    assert sorted(scheduler.released) == first_stage
+
+
+def _free_consecutive_ports(n: int) -> list[int]:
+    """N consecutive free ports, laid out like one TP1 worker per stage."""
+    for base in range(20000, 30000, 97):
+        socks = []
+        try:
+            for port in range(base, base + n):
+                sock = socket.socket()
+                socks.append(sock)
+                sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
+        except OSError:
+            continue
+        finally:
+            for sock in socks:
+                sock.close()
+        return list(range(base, base + n))
+    raise RuntimeError("no free port range")
+
+
+def _wait_for(condition, timeout: float = 10.0) -> bool:
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        if condition():
+            return True
+        time.sleep(0.01)
+    return condition()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", PARAMS_SHAPES)
+def test_every_stage_gets_the_allocation_and_release(shape, monkeypatch):

+    real sockets, with each params shape (P TP1 x PP4)."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(moriio_engine, "get_role", lambda: ROLE.PRODUCER)
+    ports = _free_consecutive_ports(4)
+    stages = []
+    for port in ports:
+        wrapper = MoRIIOWrapper()
+        wrapper.notify_port = port
+        stages.append(wrapper)
+    stages[0].stage_notify_ports = ports[1:]
+    for wrapper in stages:
+        wrapper.async_wait_reqid()
+    params = _decode_params(shape, 4, 1, host="127.0.0.1", notify_port=ports[0])
+    scheduler = _decode_scheduler(send=True)
+
+    scheduler.update_state_after_alloc(
+        SimpleNamespace(request_id="req", kv_transfer_params=params),
+        SimpleNamespace(get_block_ids=lambda: ([5, 6, 7],)),
+        num_external_tokens=40,
+    )
+    assert _wait_for(
+        lambda: all("tA" in w.done_remote_allocate_req_dict for w in stages)
+    )
+    assert all(
+        w.done_remote_allocate_req_dict["tA"].block_ids == [[5, 6, 7]] for w in stages

`pp_size` is read here, but nothing sets it. `request_finished` returns `tp_size` (L1672) but not `pp_size`. So a router that forwards the prefill's returned `kv_transfer_params` to the decode (the serial-WRITE / llm-d path described in `update_state_after_alloc`) leaves the decode thinking the prefill has PP=1.

For a TP1 x PP4 prefill, the decode then notifies only `notify_port + 0`. Stages 1-3 never get the allocation, wait `defer_timeout` (60 s), and send `write_failed`, so every request fails. I checked this with the returned keys: `get_peer_notify_ports(...)` gives `[61005]`, while the stages bind `61005..61008`.

Suggested fix: add `pp_size=self.vllm_config.parallel_config.pipeline_parallel_size,` next to `tp_size=` in `request_finished`.

A stage running on another node gets past this check. The decode sends every stage's allocation and release to one host (`remote_host`, from rank 0's heartbeat). With TP8 x PP2 across two nodes, for example, stage 1 never receives its allocation, and each request fails after `defer_timeout`.

The PR aims to fail unsupported setups at startup, so consider also refusing `parallel_config.nnodes_within_dp > 1` here when PP > 1 (this covers the mp backend). The doc should also say that all stages must share a host.
